newsitem.title: USA: Hughes Electronics earnings fall in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Hughes Electronics earnings fall in quarter.

text.p: Hughes Electronics Corp. Monday said earnings fell slightly in the third quarter, citing weakness in its aerospace and telecommunications business, as well as a higher tax rate.
The results were about in line with expectations but Hughes stock fell $1.125 to $55.75 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

Hughes, a subsidiary of General Motors Corp. that makes electronics, weapons and auto parts, said earnings fell to $252 million, or 63 cents a share, from $256.1 million, or 64 cents a share, in the 1995 quarter. Sales rose 11 percent to $3.82 billion from $3.44 billion.
Operating profit jumped 10.2 percent at Hughes' automotive electronics operations, but fell in its two other segments, aerospace and defence and telecommunications and space.
The strength in automotive electronics came on solid growth overseas and higher production volume at GM in North America, Hughes said.
Taxes rose to $144.7 million in the quarter from $121 million in the 1995 period, the Los Angeles-based company said.

Earnings for the nine months rose 7 percent to $870.3 million, or $2.18 a share, from $813.4 million, or $2.03 a share, in the 1995 period. The improvement came mainly from a gain on the sale of 2.5 percent of Hughes' DIRECTV satellite television business to AT&T.
Revenues rose 8 percent to $11.62 billion from $10.74 billion.
